question: Does equalising axis coverage across targets remove the advantage a policy gets from counting offers?
answer: No. It relocates the advantage from the count channel to the dossier-order channel at almost unchanged magnitude. Padded, every target carries seven entries, so the per-target total is constant and the policy degenerates to buying from the first-listed dossier -- which is the reference-best target in the packets as authored.
findings: coverage_static outscores the lattice on coronaviridae and henipavirus both padded and unpadded.
Padding raises coverage_static on henipavirus, from 0.6095 to 0.6761.

Unpadded, the orbit reads attributable_to_identity 0.0 and attributable_to_presentation 0.0 for coverage_static while it scores 0.7539. The nuisance group has no element that permutes how many claims a target carries, so the count channel is invisible to it and a policy exploiting that channel is certified clean.
Padded, attributable_to_presentation is 0.4279: the orbit does see the order channel, so the relocation is detectable even though the repair is not.
limitations: One orbit, three elements per kind, on one packet. A first measurement, not a result.
Padding was measured, not adopted: PAD_ABSENT_AXES defaults to False and every recorded artifact predating this file was produced unpadded.
path_note: Kept at runs/ top level rather than runs/monitor/, because runs/ is ignored wholesale and git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is also excluded. The two other artifacts tracked by exception live here for the same reason.
